October 29, 2026

US warns Gulf allies to prepare for renewed strikes on Iran after midterms

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @aaronparnas

US officials have told Middle Eastern allies to brace for possible military strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, according to diplomats cited by the Associated Press and reporting in the Wall Street Journal. Plans under consideration target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, with strikes described as a short but intense campaign possibly beginning as soon as the day after the vote. The Pentagon has deployed roughly 9,000 additional troops to the Persian Gulf, a Patriot battery is heading to Israel and another carrier strike group is due next month. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran continues to give diplomacy a chance; the conflict, which began in February, has cost an estimated $47.1 billion.

Hegseth fires the Pentagon's top war planner days before expected Iran action

tags: defence, politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Joint Staff's director for strategy, plans and policy, was removed from his post on Wednesday with no public explanation, according to The Atlantic and the Associated Press. He is the second officer forced out of the J5 role within a year, part of a broader series of senior removals under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The ouster comes as the administration weighs renewed strikes on Iran following the November 3 midterms.

Netanyahu claims Israeli election was stolen by Arab parties as his bloc loses majority

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @groundnews

Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party has accused Arab political parties of stealing Tuesday's parliamentary election, alleging bribery, threats, ballot irregularities and the use of prohibited voter-mobilisation software, and says it is submitting hundreds of testimonies to the police, the Shin Bet and the Central Elections Committee. An official from the Central Elections Committee rejected the fraud allegations in a Channel 12 interview. With about 86% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc fell from 68 seats to 53 and the opposition holds 48, leaving neither at the 61 needed to govern, while Arab-led parties Ra'am and the Joint List won a record 19 seats. Two of the four opposition parties have ruled out relying on those seats, and analysts say the likeliest outcomes are a fresh election early next year or a unity government, with Netanyahu staying on as caretaker either way.

DOJ confirms federal agents will be sent to polling places as National Guard mobilises

tags: elections, politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Justice has confirmed in a court filing that agents from the DEA, the ATF and the Federal Bureau of Prisons will be deployed to polling places for the midterm elections. The department says the personnel will observe and take notes only, will not act as law enforcement and will not carry firearms, and that FBI and ICE officials will not be present. Separately, journalist Ken Klippenstein reported that the National Guard has quietly mobilised in all 50 states, with military sources describing a mission supporting federal cybersecurity efforts in which guardsmen would observe ballot drop boxes and polling sites. The Pentagon has repeatedly told Congress that stationing guardsmen or ICE agents at the polls would be illegal.

ProPublica details Cleta Mitchell network shaping Trump election agenda

tags: elections, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A ProPublica report describes how conservative lawyer Cleta Mitchell built a grassroots network aimed at transforming American voting systems and worked closely with the Trump administration on its election agenda. At least 25 administration officials are said to have close ties to Mitchell, who helped draft the SAVE Act framework and advised on the president's election executive orders. She is now pressing for further action around the election, including unilateral enforcement of an executive-order blueprint that courts have blocked and having agencies intervene with voting machines, steps some of her own allies describe as going too far.

Flávio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's rightful leader from Miami

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich

Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's runoff to President Lula by more than four million votes, declared himself the rightful leader of Brazil from Miami on Wednesday and said he will govern and lead the opposition from the United States, comparing his position to exiled Venezuelan opposition figures. Lula won with 51.8 percent, a result recognised by Brazil's electoral court, international observers, Bolsonaro's own party and the US State Department. Bolsonaro left Brazil in defiance of a court order to surrender his passport while under investigation for money laundering, corruption and tax evasion, which he denies, and the Trump administration approved visas for him and his family within a day. Asked whether he agrees Bolsonaro is Brazil's rightful president, Trump said he would not comment; critics note the same administration plans to revoke nearly 200,000 visitor visas and has banned entry from entire countries.

Searchable database of 40,000 DHS employees published after reported hack

tags: surveillance, privacy, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A searchable database containing the names of roughly 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including undercover ICE agents, has been published following a reported hack attributed to antifascist activists. The figure represents about a third of the department's workforce. The release follows an executive order signed earlier this year designating Antifa a domestic terrorist organisation, and raises questions about the legality of the disclosure.

ICE terminations surge after record hiring push, with fired officers reporting blacklisting

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Between July 2025 and May 2026 ICE carried out the largest hiring surge in US federal law enforcement history, eliminating upper age caps, lowering the minimum applicant age to 18, offering $50,000 bonuses and reducing training and vetting standards to onboard 12,000 new agents and officers. The agency has since lost roughly 5,000 personnel, with terminations and firings now accounting for 73% of all separations compared with 16% in previous years. One recently terminated deportation officer said he can never work in federal law enforcement again and that local police departments will not hire him because ICE appears on his résumé, and some former hires are reportedly being asked to repay their signing bonuses.

US strike on Eastern Pacific boat kills five as toll passes 230

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

US forces struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific, killing five people, according to US Southern Command. SOUTHCOM said the go-fast boat was travelling an established trafficking route and cited confirmed intelligence linking it to drug trafficking. Reuters reports that such strikes have killed more than 230 people since September 2025, and rights groups describe them as unlawful killings.

Army rehearses mass temporary burials at Fort Bragg

tags: war, defence
sources: @total.hypocrisy

According to the Army Times, engineers, preventative medicine teams, chaplains and fatality management specialists practised mass temporary interment during an exercise at Fort Bragg in North Carolina, a capability not used on a large scale since the Korean War. The Army said chaplains from various faith groups were consulted on consecrating burial sites in advance, because in an operational environment the identities or faith backgrounds of fallen service members may not be known. The exercise has been linked to preparations for renewed military operations against Iran, including possible action around Kharg Island.

Texts show Peltola campaign helped recruit second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race

tags: elections, politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Text messages obtained by The New York Times show that the campaign of Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola discussed recruiting a candidate named Dan Sullivan to run against Alaska's Republican incumbent of the same name, potentially confusing voters. The campaign recruited retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan, who advanced through the August primary and remains on the ballot after the state Supreme Court ruled he met constitutional eligibility requirements, despite state election officials seeking to disqualify him. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee denied involvement despite appearing in the reported messages. President Trump has directed the Justice Department to challenge certification of a potential Peltola victory, citing the second Sullivan's candidacy.

Trump administration strips roughly 90% of Bears Ears National Monument

tags: environment, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A new proclamation has removed roughly 90% of the acreage of Bears Ears National Monument in southern Utah and dissolved the Bears Ears Inter-Tribal Commission, the body that made tribally led management possible. Diné leaders Angelo Baca and Natasha Hale, writing in High Country News, say the move threatens petroglyphs and ancestral sites and would open the door to unravelling protections for any national monument in the country. They argue that land management should instead place Indigenous leadership in the driver's seat, and that uncertainty is being deliberately introduced into a vision tribes spent a decade building with the Bureau of Land Management.

HF Sinclair pipeline would run under Salt Lake area drinking water

tags: environment, energy, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Draft maps filed with Salt Lake City show HF Sinclair plans a new fuel pipeline crossing under Silver Creek in Summit County, running through Parleys and down Emigration Canyon, then following the foothills above the University of Utah. Surveyors appeared in open space near residents' homes last week; hundreds of families in Emigration Canyon draw water from private wells, more than 1,200 people have signed a petition against the route, and Salt Lake City's mayor and city council have said they are deeply concerned about the city's drinking water and the Great Salt Lake. The company has told investors the fuel is destined for Nevada and California, and the full project could move 150,000 barrels a day; it reported $2 billion in profit in a single quarter, four times the prior year. An existing corridor down Weber Canyon could be upgraded instead, but that would require months of downtime, and a law passed by the Utah Legislature this year speeds up pipeline permits and leaves counties without a veto over the route.

Utah still lacks dust monitoring as drying Great Salt Lake exposes residents to toxic metals

tags: health, environment
sources: @carolinegleich

Dust blowing off the drying Great Salt Lake carries arsenic, lead and uranium, and laboratory tests show the metals in that dust enter the lungs more readily than those in ordinary dust and remain in leafy greens even after washing. Children and older adults face the greatest risk, with lead capable of causing lasting damage to a developing brain. Four years after the lake hit its record low, the state has no real-time dust monitors the public can check and no funded alert system, and consumer PurpleAir sensors barely register the large particles involved. Utah's top air quality official recently described the lake as a future issue.

Britain pledges a further £10 billion in support for Ukraine

tags: war, defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Finance minister John Healey told lawmakers on Wednesday that Britain will provide Ukraine with an additional £10 billion in support, according to Reuters. The package comprises £7 billion in economic support over three years, £3 billion in export finance capacity and £500 million in urgent military funding for this winter. Downing Street said the military money will address urgent gaps in Ukraine's air defences.

Ethiopia receives 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said on Wednesday that Ethiopia has taken delivery of 12 Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets, according to Reuters, and that four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow will follow. Abiy said President Vladimir Putin helped deliver the aircraft a year ahead of schedule. The deliveries come as Ethiopia faces renewed fighting in Tigray and a rupture with Eritrea, which Addis Ababa accuses of backing rebels.

Fire breaks out at Savannah River nuclear complex in South Carolina

tags: energy, environment
sources: @total.hypocrisy

A fire broke out at the Department of Energy's Savannah River Site in South Carolina on the evening of October 28. The fire was extinguished, traffic was barred from the area, airspace over the facility was closed and nearby rail traffic was halted. Reports from the site indicated no impact outside the facility. The complex produced materials for nuclear weapons during the Cold War and is now used for environmental stewardship and the disposal of nuclear waste.

Heckler shouts about Epstein plane at Trump rally in Ohio

tags: politics, epstein
sources: @aaronparnas

A heckler interrupted a Trump rally in Ohio, shouting that the president had been on Jeffrey Epstein's plane. Trump responded angrily from the stage, claiming the protester had been paid $250 to attend. The interruption came during a stretch of remarks in which the president was commenting on a sitting senator's appearance.

Musk attack on Talarico draws Epstein email comparison

tags: epstein, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Elon Musk posted on X that there is "something deeply wrong" with Talarico. The post drew a response pointing to Musk's own correspondence with Jeffrey Epstein, specifically a reported email asking Epstein which night his wildest party would be.

Missile defence systems installed at Mar-a-Lago ahead of elections

tags: defence, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The US military has installed surface-to-air missile systems outside Mar-a-Lago, Donald Trump's Palm Beach club, ahead of next week's elections and possible renewed military action against Iran. A photograph of the systems was taken by the Palm Beach Post. The deployment reflects concerns about the president being targeted that date to the Butler, Pennsylvania shooting.

Obama attacks on prices and corruption rattle Republican midterm strategy

tags: politics, elections, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Barack Obama escalated his criticism of the Trump administration, saying it had not disputed his claims that it is directly responsible for rising prices, that tariffs are contributing to higher household costs, or that it is engaged in unprecedented corruption. He said the administration instead mounted a whole-of-government response to a joke about the Cheesecake Factory, including arranging for the treasury secretary to hold a press conference outside one of the restaurants. Republican operatives warn that the president is now more focused on responding to Obama than on an affordability message heading into November, with the campaign posting memes in reply and Obama drawing crowds of about 10,000 compared with one to two thousand at a competing Trump event.

Trump says he would nominate Ted Cruz to the Supreme Court

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

At an October 27 rally in Lubbock, Texas, President Trump said he would pick Senator Ted Cruz for a future Supreme Court vacancy, joking that both parties would vote to confirm him because they want him gone, according to USA Today. Cruz, seated in the front row, laughed at the remark. He has previously said he does not want to be a judge.

ICE deletes AI-generated recruitment post after mocking 60 Minutes report

tags: immigration, media
sources: @oafnation_actual

The official ICEgov account posted, then deleted, a recruitment advertisement featuring an AI-generated image of shirtless deportation officers with the caption "Hit Arms, Join ICE, Save America." It followed a post a day earlier responding to a 60 Minutes report about Moussa Diawara, a Malian national detained by ICE and deported to Ghana; the agency called the report "Fake & Gay!" and alleged immigration fraud over his asylum claim of persecution as a homosexual man. The posts drew widespread criticism, and agency officials have said the department's use of social media is damaging ICE's image.

Israeli military courts convict Palestinian children at near-total rate, UNICEF found

tags: legal, war
sources: @ericmoutsos

Palestinian children detained for throwing stones are tried in a military court near Jerusalem, where according to the courts' own annual report the conviction rate is around 99.74% and some hearings last 60 seconds. A boy convicted of stone-throwing is typically sentenced to about three months in prison, with reported sentences ranging considerably longer. A UNICEF report found that Palestinian children had been threatened with death, physical violence, solitary confinement and sexual assault against themselves or family members, and concluded that ill treatment was widespread, systematic and institutionalised from arrest through sentencing.
